verifier_note: Checked every recipe's warrant sources by direct retrieval (curl/gh api, never memory): docs.rs pages at the pinned crate versions, doc.rust-lang.org at stable/1.98.1, the RFC and WASM spec, crates.io publish dates, and si-rpg-engine's actual source (README.md, packages/tick/tick.js, packages/frame/hash.js, harness/*, solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, solver/build.mjs, docs/dispatch-*.md, fixtures/golden-behaviour.json, CHANGELOG.md), fetched at both the pinned commit 1701b72 and main HEAD be0ea06 (byte-identical for every Rust/JS file checked, so no drift). Both mandated high-stakes checks were independently reproduced with the compile oracle using the engine's own mixer/lane code copied verbatim from rapier_law.rs and hash.js, not the recipe's supplied source: the mix_u64 signature mixer collides on the named half-extent pair (d1b28807b4eb6fed both) while FNV-1a64 and xxh3_64 do not, and any u32-only stream through the two-lane hasher produces identical halves structurally, for arbitrary inputs. Two more compile_fail claims (E0277 on ColliderHandle.sort(), E0004 on a Mode match missing Carried) were also independently reproduced. Essentially every one of the ~90 warrant-source claims checked matched its retrieved page at a verbatim or near-verbatim level; only one defect was found, a minor misattribution in recipe 1 (the 'f64 cannot represent every Duration' sentence belongs to Duration::mul_f64's docs, not from_secs_f64's, though from_secs_f64 does round as its own examples show). All primary sources are dated 2024 or later, meeting the recency bar. The systemic weakness: six of the crates this lane leans on for engine-facing claims -- bevy_time, ggrs, backroll, blake3, bevy_ecs and hecs -- are absent from the compile oracle's ORACLE_DEPS set (rapier3d_f64, parry3d_f64, bytemuck, slotmap, indexmap, serde_json and a few others are the only crates the oracle can actually build and run against). Every claim touching those six crates is verified by reading a documentation page, never by a compiled call into the real crate; recipe 10's only check explicitly says as much ('neither is in the oracle set, so the check models the mechanism'). My own page-reads back every one of those claims solidly, but the lane's own mechanical verification floor -- the thing meant to catch a hallucinated method name or signature without a human or model rereading prose -- silently does not reach about a third of the crates it cites.
